question.text: What is the regulatory position on co-location services for ETIRD trading?

answer.text: Exchanges offer co-location/proximity hosting to stock brokers and data vendors, allowing systems near exchange premises with direct/private network connection
Co-location is banned by SEBI for all derivative segments
Only government-owned brokers can use co-location
Co-location is available only for equity trading, not IRD

explanation.text: The Logic: Per NISM Series IV (p.196), exchanges offer co-location/proximity hosting services to stock brokers and data vendors, allowing them to place their systems near the exchange premises with direct/private network connectivity for faster order execution. The Trap: Co-location is not banned and is not restricted to government-owned brokers. The text confirms availability of co-location/proximity hosting; broader claims about uniform fair-access guarantees or availability across all derivative segments require separate sourcing. Note: Co-location provides latency advantages used by algorithmic traders; SEBI guidelines around access and pricing are governed by separate circulars beyond this checked page.
